newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon's Bongo and U.N. envoy discuss Congo crisis.
newsitem.headline: Gabon's Bongo and U.N. envoy discuss Congo crisis.

text.p: U.N. envoy Mohamed Sahnoun met Gabon's veteran president, Omar Bongo, on Thursday after making a flying visit to the Congo Republic's divided capital and sounding out the warring parties there, officials said.
No details emerged from the meeting between the two men, who have been trying to mediate a lasting end to ethnic and political bloodshed that broke out in Brazzaville on June 5.
In Brazzaville, a 72-hour truce held for a second day.

"I insisted very strongly that this ceasefire should be respected and not only for three days but beyond that," Sahnoun said on Wednesday after talks with President Pascal Lissouba and former military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso.

"The political leaders assured me that they would give instructions to their troops and to their military negotiators to prolong the ceasefire as long as possible," he told journalists before leaving Brazzaville.

At the same time, Sahnoun called for an intervention force and urged France to keep some troops in Brazzaville until such a force could arrive. "I think the problem is going to be when the peace force can be deployed. I'm much more afraid of the vacuum that could exist in the short term," he said.
Sahnoun also met Brazzaville mayor Bernard Kolelas, the third force in town whose militia have kept out of the fighting so far and who is also acting as a mediator.
Bongo, Sahnoun and the presidents of Mali, Chad and Central African Republic met envoys of all sides in Libreville on Monday but failed to find enough common ground to forge a deal.
